$comment: Explicit, checked-in record of optional capabilities (spec/manifest.json's optional_capabilities) that the bounded C++ host does not yet declare `supported`. Read by tools/spec_runner/host_parity_gate.py. Each entry's `capability` must be a name from spec/manifest.json's optional_capabilities list and must include reason, tracking_issue, affected_host, affected_tests, and removal_condition. An optional capability the C++ host declares `unsupported` (or does not declare at all) that is NOT listed here fails the host-parity CI gate as an undocumented gap. An entry here whose capability the C++ host now declares `supported` also fails the gate (a stale entry) until this file is updated. This file makes no portable-semantics claim of its own -- see docs/releases/R24.md and docs/releases/R25.md for the authoritative evidence it summarizes.

gaps.reason: Deferred out of R27 by E27-3 (docs/analysis/r27-http-server-decision.md): the HTTP server is a Python-host-only blocking bridge with no shared evidence route, and the bounded C++ host lacks import, annotations, a serve mode, and sockets.
affected_tests: HTTP server requires-gated shared specs (none exist yet)
gaps.removal_condition: Remove only after a separate contract-first HTTP-server release defines portable shared evidence, genia-cpp declares http_server supported, and the host parity gate reports the capability as PARITY_OK.

gaps.reason: Deferred out of R27 by E27-4 (docs/analysis/r27-outbound-http-decision.md): outbound HTTP has no Genia surface of its own, needs host-minted R10 declassification authority and runner fixture plumbing the shared protocol lacks, and the bounded C++ host lacks import, protected values, lifecycle scopes, and sockets.
affected_tests: HTTP outbound transport requires-gated shared specs (none exist yet)
gaps.removal_condition: Remove only after a separate contract-first outbound-HTTP release defines portable authority and fixture evidence, genia-cpp declares http_outbound_transport supported, and the host parity gate reports the capability as PARITY_OK.

gaps.reason: docs/design/r26-cpp-data-bridge-contract.md section 5 decided compatibility JSON (json_parse/json_stringify/json_pretty) and parse_jsonl_record are NOT portable and remain Python-host-only, so their previously-ungated shared cases are now retro-gated behind this capability. This is a permanent host-local classification by design, not an in-progress gap awaiting C++ implementation, unless a future contract revision explicitly makes compatibility JSON portable.
gaps.removal_condition: Not expected to be removed by C++ implementation, since this capability is decided Python-host-only by contract. Remove only if a future contract revision makes compatibility JSON portable, genia-cpp then declares json_compat supported, and the host parity gate reports the capability as PARITY_OK.

gaps.reason: The bounded C++ host does not parse or lower the `=:` immutable-declaration token and has no Env binding-policy enforcement (Model B Slice B). Python is the reference implementation; this is an honest optional-capability gap, not parity. The C++ parser/lowering work is owned by m0smith/genia-cpp#50.
gaps.removal_condition: Remove when genia-cpp lowers IrImmutableBind, enforces the shared immutable-binding policy, declares immutable_bindings supported, and the host parity gate reports the capability as PARITY_OK.

gaps.reason: Model B Slice C (default-open ordinary function execution, pattern/guard-headed ordinary functions, unified shape-stratum dispatch, ownership diagnostics) is implemented by the Python reference host for issue #1269; the pinned C++ host does not declare the capability. The nine shared failures originally tracked separately in m0smith/genia-cpp#53 through #57 now pass at reviewed C++ pin 1af65fd2425526573f9ca765b3a027e37dfa5c74. Issues #55 through #57 are closed; #53 remains open for positive guard/nested-arm acceptance and #54 for its guard-differs criterion. Unsupported guard rejection does not satisfy those criteria. This capability gap does not waive actual failures or the remaining issue acceptance requirements: final Slice C merge requires zero actual failure classes in the selected C++ host's exact shared conformance run.
gaps.removal_condition: Remove only after genia-cpp declares default_open_functions supported, passes every case listed here with zero failure classes on the exact final conformance YAML and pin, and the host parity gate reports the capability as PARITY_OK.
